speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms, could you tell me which antibiotic you were taking and approximately how long before the rash and joint pain appeared? Also, have you noticed any swelling or redness in the joints, or is it just pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash distribution in the flexural areas and its onset one week after starting amoxicillin strongly suggest a serum sickness-like reaction. I will confirm this by checking for any other systemic symptoms. Do you have any swelling of the hands, feet, or face, or have you noticed any changes in your urination?

speaker: Doctor
text: The lack of additional symptoms and the classic presentation confirm my suspicion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Serum sickness-like reaction
